newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWAY'S PGS, AWILCO PLAN MERGER - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY'S PGS, AWILCO PLAN MERGER - REPORT.

text.p: Norwegian offshore services companies Petroleum Geo-Services ASA (PGS) and Awilco ASA are looking to merge operations during 1997, financial news magazine Kapital said on Thursday.
Synergies between the two could be considerable and the new merged company would be well prepared for further growth, Kapital said.
Rumors of a merger between PGS and Awilco have been circulating in the market for some time. Kapital said representatives from the two companies had used the summer break to work on a solution.
PGS declined to comment on the report.
"The rumours are old and we have nothing to say about rumours," said PGS financial director Morten Lunde. "There is nothing new from our side."

Kapital said Awilco's company structure complicated a direct merger between Awilco or Awilco division Spekter Golar Nor and PGS. A merger between PGS and Petrojarl 4DA, another Awilco division, was not possible under company law, it said.

"Therefore it is likely that there will be a demerger in Awilco, whereby a new company will be established. Awilco shareholders will get shares in the new (demerged) company. The most important assets of the new company will be in (Awilco divisions and subsidiaries) Spekter GNO and Petrojarl 4...
"After the demerger is completed the plan is to merge PGS into the new company, where the shareholders will be given PGS shares."
Kapital said a demerger in Awilco, formation of a new company and the subsequent merger with PGS would require two advisories to shareholders, each of which would take two months.
"The partners therefore aim to complete the merger by the end of 1997. Orkla Finans and Salomon Brothers are provisionally advisers for the merger process," it said.

"Many companies would gladly jump into bed with PGS. If the merger with Awilco goes ahead, the new merged unit could also attract further marriages. Maybe we will see a new offshore company including PGS, Awilco and Aker Maritime? Such a structure would really prove a test for the oil companies.
"But first the PGS/Awilco fusion must be in place. The North Sea will be an exciting playground in the future," Kapital said.
